mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (each >1.0% monthly) signal broad consumer demand contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline >1.0% monthly, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Early-cycle industrial production growth exceeding 2.0% YoY supports economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion (INDPRO >2.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS <4.0%), S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: CPI year-over-year growth exceeding 3.0% signals rising inflation, prompting monetary tightening expectations and negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3.0%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly payroll growth exceeding 100k reflects labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent low interest rates (FEDFUNDS <2.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY >3.0%) create a monetary policy dilemma, increasing volatility and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS <2.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY >3.0%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Early expansion GDP growth exceeding 3.0% annualized supports corporate earnings momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In early expansion (GDPC1 annualized growth >3.0% and FEDFUNDS <4.0%), S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
